sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx:Quality Checks row 36 (quality check 35); Internal Quality Checks row 36
evidence: The defining edit-and-run behavior is tested by the Render gate: gates/render/judge.toml:18-23 requires authored keyboard-entered JavaScript, Run, and two button clicks with increasing preview and console results. Server readback after a Save, clean context, and reload is tested by gates/constraints/judge.toml:27-32. The public requirement explicitly says saved work and history survive a complete server restart (environment/instructions/behaviour.md:9; integration.md:7), and scored/functional/judge.toml:198-203 tries to grade that by calling restart_app. However that functional judge declares only the Playwright MCP server at lines 8-12 and starts [scoring] at line 14; it omits the verifier MCP server required by the frozen staged-task-contract.md and present in the frozen template functional judge.toml. test.sh:193 exports APP_RESTART_HELPER, but exporting it does not expose restart_app to the judge. Thus reload and clean-context persistence are graded, while the required complete-process restart is not executable through the configured functional judge. No raw-evidence-index.json or full configured judge log was present in the run root when reviewed; runtime confirmation remains unmeasured.
counterexample: An app keeps snippets in server process memory. It can pass the Render gate and the Constraints gate's fresh-context/reload readback while the process stays alive, yet lose all saved work on restart. The functional judge cannot call restart_app because its MCP server is absent, so it cannot distinguish that broken app from a durable one; a fully durable app also cannot furnish the requested restart observation through this configuration.
suggested_fix: Add the frozen template's verifier MCP server block to tests/scored/functional/judge.toml, with /tests/tools/restart_mcp.py and $APP_RESTART_HELPER, then run the configured judge and retain logs proving a successful process restart and fresh-page readback; report tool failure as missing evidence, not an app failure.
